## Research Question

Do Moltbook agents adapt their linguistic style when expressing semantically similar ideas across different submolts
(communities)? How does their rhetorical or stylistic expression change depending on the submolt?

## Data Source

We use the **Moltbook Observatory Archive** on Hugging Face ([dataset card][hf-moltbook-archive]): an incremental
export of the Moltbook Observatory SQLite database, published as date-partitioned Parquet for browsing and
programmatic access. Each observatory table is exposed as a **subset** (configuration) of the same dataset id. We
load **`agents`**, **`posts`**, and **`submolts`** for agent metadata, post text and scores, and submolt (community)
metadata respectively, matching the table descriptions on the dataset card.

The archive is derived from periodic snapshots of the **passive** Moltbook Observatory system (observe-only, no
posting); see the live dashboard and upstream code for context ([GitHub][molt-gh], [live instance][molt-live]).

**Attribution.** Dataset and tooling by **Sushant Gautam** and **Michael A. Riegler** (SimulaMet / Hugging Face
Datasets, 2026), as listed on the dataset page **Contributors** section.

**License.** The dataset card specifies the **MIT** license; retain notices and the license text when redistributing
derived artifacts.

[hf-moltbook-archive]: https://huggingface.co/datasets/SimulaMet/moltbook-observatory-archive
[molt-gh]: https://github.com/kelkalot/moltbook-observatory
[molt-live]: https://moltbook-observatory.sushant.info.np/

### Download Datasets

The [`datasets`][hf-datasets] library from Hugging Face provides **`load_dataset`**, a single entry point that
downloads (or streams) a dataset repository from the Hub, reads the dataset script or Parquet layout, and returns a
**`DatasetDict`** keyed by split names (often just `train`). You pass the **dataset id** (`org/name`), an optional
**subset** when the repo defines multiple configurations (here `agents`, `posts`, `submolts`), and flags such as
**`trust_remote_code=True`** when loading relies on custom code approved for this run. Below, results are converted
to **pandas** `DataFrame`s and written to Parquet under `data/` for faster local reuse.

[hf-datasets]: https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/

::: {#setup-paths .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from pathlib import Path


def repo_root() -> Path:
    """Identifies Repository root (directory with requirements.txt)"""
    cwd = Path.cwd().resolve()
    if (cwd / "requirements.txt").exists():
        return cwd
    if (cwd.parent / "requirements.txt").exists():
        return cwd.parent
    return cwd


ROOT = repo_root()
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

print("ROOT    :", ROOT)
print("DATA_DIR:", DATA_DIR)
```

::: {#load-hf .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from datasets import load_dataset
import pandas as pd

HF_DATASET = "SimulaMet/moltbook-observatory-archive"
LOAD_KW = {"trust_remote_code": True}


def to_df(ds):
    """One DataFrame per dataset; all splits concatenated."""
    splits = list(ds.keys())
    if len(splits) == 1:
        return ds[splits[0]].to_pandas()
    return pd.concat([ds[s].to_pandas() for s in splits], ignore_index=True)


ds_agents = load_dataset(HF_DATASET, "agents", **LOAD_KW)
ds_posts = load_dataset(HF_DATASET, "posts", **LOAD_KW)
ds_submolts = load_dataset(HF_DATASET, "submolts", **LOAD_KW)

df_agents = to_df(ds_agents)
df_posts = to_df(ds_posts)
df_submolts = to_df(ds_submolts)

print("df_agents  ", df_agents.shape)
print("df_posts   ", df_posts.shape)
print("df_submolts", df_submolts.shape)
```

## Project Objective

This section loads **posts** (preferring the raw Parquet written above), filters highly repetitive automated `mbc-20`
crypto blocks, and saves a processed Parquet checkpoint under `data/` at the repository root.

::: {#setup-repo-paths .cell message='false' execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from datasets import load_dataset


def repo_root() -> Path:
    cwd = Path.cwd().resolve()
    if (cwd / "requirements.txt").exists():
        return cwd
    if (cwd.parent / "requirements.txt").exists():
        return cwd.parent
    return cwd


ROOT = repo_root()
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
PROCESSED_DATA_PATH = DATA_DIR / "moltbook_cleaned.parquet"
RAW_POSTS_PATH = DATA_DIR / "posts-raw.parquet"
```
:::


::: {#load-and-clean .cell message='false' execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
if os.path.exists(PROCESSED_DATA_PATH):
    print("Found processed checkpoint — loading from disk...")
    df = pd.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DATA_PATH)
elif RAW_POSTS_PATH.exists():
    print("Loading posts from raw Parquet (HF fetch step)...")
    df = pd.read_parquet(RAW_POSTS_PATH)
else:
    print("No Parquet found — loading posts from Hugging Face...")
    dataset = load_dataset("SimulaMet/moltbook-observatory-archive", name="posts", trust_remote_code=True)
    splits = list(dataset.keys())
    if len(splits) == 1:
        df = dataset[splits[0]].to_pandas()
    else:
        df = pd.concat([dataset[s].to_pandas() for s in splits], ignore_index=True)

text_col = "content" if "content" in df.columns else ("body" if "body" in df.columns else None)
if text_col is None:
    raise ValueError(f"No text column found; columns: {list(df.columns)}")

print(f"Dataset loaded: {len(df):,} rows.  text_col={text_col!r}")
```

::: {#filter-mbc20 .cell message='false' execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Regex for automated MBC-20 / BRC-20 style JSON blocks
mbc20_pattern = re.compile(r'\{\s*"p"\s*:\s*"mbc-20".*?\}', re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)

df["is_crypto_spam"] = df[text_col].fillna("").apply(lambda x: bool(mbc20_pattern.search(str(x))))
spam_count = df["is_crypto_spam"].sum()
df_cleaned = df[~df["is_crypto_spam"]].copy()
df_cleaned.drop(columns=["is_crypto_spam"], inplace=True)

print(f"Cleaned out {spam_count:,} automated mbc-20-style rows.")
print(f"Retained {len(df_cleaned):,} posts.")

df_cleaned.to_parquet(PROCESSED_DATA_PATH, index=False)
print(f"Checkpoint saved to: {PROCESSED_DATA_PATH}")

df = df_cleaned
```
